answers.question: Question 16: You said: "Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded." The rules now act on the first lookup that gets no answer, and nothing would end retries with no limit. I propose one bound for every lookup, changing three rules. R-01, before: "When the lookup gets no answer, the agent tells the customer it cannot look up the orders now and changes nothing." After: "When the lookup gets no answer, the agent sends it once more; when that also gets no answer, the agent tells the customer it cannot look up the orders now and changes nothing." R-07, before: "If that lookup gets no answer, or the second cancel call also times out, ..." After: "If that lookup gets no answer twice in a row, or the second cancel call also times out, ..." R-08, before: "a lookup with no answer is handed to staff, and the customer is told the status is unknown." After: "a lookup that gets no answer twice in a row is handed to staff, and the customer is told the status is unknown." The shortest path where it matters: the customer asks to cancel an order; the lookup gets no answer; under the change the agent sends it once more before telling the customer it cannot look up the orders now. Do you accept the change? Claims put to the owner: C-50.
answers.recommended: Yes: every lookup that gets no answer is sent once more, and only a second no answer in a row counts as the lookup getting no answer.
answers.reply: > Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: Question 17: R-08 does not say how many refund calls the agent sends in all. Before: "When it returns a transient error, the agent sends it once more. When it times out, the agent sends it once more, then looks up the order and its refund and reports what it finds:" After: "When it returns a transient error, the agent sends it once more. When it times out, the agent sends it once more. The agent sends the refund call at most twice. When either call timed out and the second call returns no refund, the agent looks up the order and its refund and reports what it finds:" The shortest path where it matters: the order is cancelled; the refund call returns a transient error; the second refund call times out. Under the current text the agent would send a third refund call; under the change it sends no third call and looks up the refund. Do you accept the change?
answers.recommended: Yes: at most two refund calls, and a look-up of the refund whenever a time-out leaves the refund unknown.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> One retry allowed on a transient error, none on a terminal one.
> 3. Cancel succeeded, refund call timed out — state unknown; agent retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds.
> Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.
